title: Grove's inflow caps cluster into 50m, 20m and 5m tiers that track network and deployment maturity rather than venue-specific analysis
content:
Reading the inflow limits across chunks reveals a small set of repeated values rather than a distribution. Established chains take the top tier: Ripple RLUSD and Avalanche Centrifuge JTRSY and JAAA and the Avalanche Curve LP Instance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.2.2.2.2.4.1) are each 50,000,000. The newer networks take a uniform middle tier: Base Morpho Grove x Steakhouse (.3.1.1.2.4.1), Base Steakhouse Prime (.3.2.2.4.1), Plasma Aave v3 USDT0 (.4.1.1.2.4.1) and Plume Centrifuge ACRDX (.5.1.1.2.4.1) are all 20,000,000. Interim Deployments take the bottom tier at 5,000,000.

Four different protocols — Morpho, Aave, Centrifuge — across three chains that share nothing but being recent arrivals all receive precisely the same cap. That is not what independently derived limits look like.

The implied policy is a maturity ladder: the cap is a function of how proven the *network* is, with the protocol's own characteristics handled elsewhere. There is a coherent rationale for it. On a young chain, the dominant risks — sequencer failure, bridge compromise, thin liquidity, immature tooling — are properties of the chain and apply equally to whatever is deployed on it, so a chain-level cap addresses the dominant term.

The cost is that the tier can substitute for the analysis rather than bound it. Two Base Morpho vaults with different underlying loan books receive the same 20,000,000, and the tier gives no signal about which is riskier. Tiering also creates a quiet cliff: promoting a network from 20,000,000 to 50,000,000 re-rates every Instance on it simultaneously, so a single judgement about a chain propagates to allocations that were never individually reconsidered.

The tiers are also the natural place to look for drift. Any Instance whose cap does not sit on a tier boundary — Agora AUSD at 10,000,000, for example — is carrying a venue-specific judgement, and is worth reading closely for the reason.
description: Ethereum and Avalanche conduits get 50m, the newer Base, Plasma and Plume chains uniformly get 20m, and Interim Deployments get 5m — the same figures recur across unrelated protocols.
